$comment: TEST FIXTURE for src/canon/lint.test.ts -- a copy of the rules a consumer's prose-lint contract carries, under a neutral contract id so it never claims to be any consumer's single home of its rules. The consumer's own contract is its data; `nen canon lint` presupposes the consumer has landed one (Hatsu's lands with its SDD piece P5). Synced with Hatsu's committed contract at its main 1243b272 (zheref/nen#481). Not shipped.
authority: HR-13 (ratchet, PL-03 and PL-04 empty from day one; code fences and quoted maintainer words exempt) and HR-4 (the one marker shape) in docs/ROSTER.md. Where this file and a page describing it disagree, this file is right.

paths.$include: Globs over the root: `*` matches one path segment, `**` any number. surfaces/** is generated and never linted, whatever this list says.

exemptions.$exemptions: HR-13: fenced code and quoted words ("…", “…”, *"…"*) are exempt from every rule. Blockquotes and frontmatter are linted.

records.$records: Dated evidence and history records: a version literal there is what was true when it was written. docs/ROSTER.md is one because a ruling's words are never changed after it lands (HR-2). RETIRED blocks are exempt from retired.rules wherever they sit.

retired.$retired: The rules a RETIRED block (a `> **RETIRED…` quote, a `**RETIRED` paragraph or list item) is exempt from, wherever it sits: what it retired was true when it was written. A `para` block ends at a blank line, a heading or a list item at the same or a shallower indent.

$markerRows: HR-4: a marker names an ask-once-per-run row of decisionsFile, and only these; the guard refuses a contract that lists a row of any other class at exit 2, and a marker naming a human-gate row is a finding (a gate is a stop, not a question).

rules.summary: An affirmative by-hand admission: a step the plane performs by hand. A clause that refuses or retires the hand step is not one.
'until nen' or 'pending port' with no zheref/nen#N in the same paragraph ('until nen 0.7' is history, not a residue).

A claim of the current nen pin (`pin vX.Y`, `pinned nen vX.Y`, `at the pinned vX.Y`) or a nen floor (`nen vX.Y+`, `needs nen vX.Y`), outside RETIRED blocks and records, that is not the contract's minimum or pinned_ref read at run time. A provenance literal (`nen 0.19, zheref/nen#357`: the release a behaviour arrived in) is adoption history, and so is a pin claim after a past word.
A linked `§ N`, a linked `§ *Title*` or a relative link that resolves to no heading, explicit anchor or bold paragraph lead in its target, or to no file inside the root.
A bare #N with no repository code (zheref/<repo>#N, HA#N, HA-PR-#N).
'verified live', 'checked live' or 'verified against' without both a date and an evidence path in the same paragraph.
A hedge where a rule should state what happens.
A numeric flag value on a `nen …` line that matches no value declared in the declaredValues files.
A Residue item that cites neither zheref/<repo>#N nor the literal 'unfiled' (PROCESS § Residue and owned dependencies).

An open question not in the shape [NEEDS <row-id>: question], a marker naming a row outside markerRows (a human-gate row is a stop, not a question), a marker with no ledger reference (OPEN-n or zheref/<repo>#N) in its paragraph, or more than markerLimit markers in one skill.
A skill, persona or rules file citing an HR row whose status is `reading` without the word 'reading' in the same paragraph (HR-3).
